To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the number of the stages of the prescaling counter should be a variable function of the content of the prescaler, which should be chosen in such a way that the statistical error of the counter is minimum.

the prescaler should be inserted in the counter only when the number of events is greater than a threshold value that is a function of the expected number of events, the statistical error, and the number of bits of the exponent section.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and implementation of variable prescaling counters for spaceborne experiments.
the design of a variable prescaling counter that is capable of operating with a variable number of stages.
the development of new design techniques for variable prescaling counters, which are able to adapt the number of inserted prescaling stages to the actual content of the exponent counter.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, if a prescaling counter is used for the automatic compression on board of a spacecraft, the best choice is the one that is based on the proposed new design technique, which takes into account the statistical errors, and that is implemented in the way that the number of stages is an arbitrary function, and not a fixed function, of the content of the prescaling counter.
the use of the standard technique of realizing the logarithmic counter, where the exponent section is always filled up with the same number of stages of prescalers, is not always the best solution.

, in the case of a random source, the best technique is the use of an adaptive prescaling counter, whose number of stages depends on the content of the counter itself and on the number of expected events.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in the case of a random source, a logarithmic counter is not the best choice.
we have shown the way to a more rational design of the prescaling counters, where the number and type of stages are chosen in such a way that the overall performance of the system is optimized.

, if the expected number of events to be recorded is known a priori with sufficient accuracy, it is possible to design a prescaling counter that is more efficient and that has a lower hardware complexity than the standard one, and that is also more robust to variations of the actual number of events.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, by properly designing the function that determines the number of stages inserted into the prescaler, it is possible to achieve a significant reduction of the number of bits required for the representation of the data, without any increase of the error probability of the measurement.

the prescaling counters should be designed in such a way that the statistical error in the number of events counted is minimized, which is achieved by minimizing the number of events that are lost in the compression process.
a logarithmic counter can be designed in such a way that the statistical error is minimized and the number of bits in the exponent section is minimized as well.
